records.context: 1. **Flatten.** Denoise with a 1 px Gaussian, then subtract a heavily smoothed copy (sigma = max(32, min(H, W) / 4)) to remove illumination gradients. The sigma is deliberately far larger than any plausible object so that flattening removes vignetting without removing the objects — the opposite trade-off (a tight rolling ball) shrinks what it is trying to measure. 2. **Reject noise.** Compare the structural amplitude of the flattened plane (p99 - p30) against the *pixel-level* noise scale, measured as ``1.4826 * MAD(img - gaussian(img, 1))`` on the raw plane. A pure-noise plane scores below 1; a plane with real objects scores in the tens. Below ``min_snr`` the field is discarded rather than thresholded, because Otsu returns a threshold even for pure noise, and the resulting size looks valid. 3. **Threshold and label.** Otsu, fill holes, label, drop components that touch the image border (truncated, so their size is too small) and components that are absurd (equivalent diameter below ``min_object_diameter``, or area above ``max_object_fraction`` of the field). Sizes are equivalent diameters, ``2 * sqrt(area / pi)``. 4. **Drop specks, then take the median.** A textured or punctate stain (a mitochondrial cell stain, a parasite marker) thresholds into a few whole objects plus hundreds of 4-10 px specks, and a plain median counts every speck as an object: on spaCR's own test laboratory microplate that put the cell at 8 px and the pathogen at 11 px against 175 px and 32 px in the curated masks, while the nucleus, whose stain is solid, came out right at 91 px. So the typical object is first located by the stained area it carries (the area-weighted median, which specks cannot move because they hold almost no area), everything narrower than :data:`SPECK_FRACTION` of it is dropped, and the characteristic size is the median of what remains. Small components that together hold :data:`SPECK_MAX_AREA_SHARE` of the stained area or more are a second population, not specks, and stay. 5. **Cross-check by distance transform.** Step 3 has one dominant failure mode: a confluent monolayer fuses into a single component, that component touches the border and is dropped, and the estimate is then computed from whatever debris survived — biased **low**, and silently. So the Euclidean distance transform of the (unfilled) foreground is computed as well, its local maxima are taken as one seed per object (two passes: a coarse pass sets the suppression radius for the refined pass), and a watershed on ``-EDT`` splits the fused foreground back into objects whose equivalent diameters are measured the same way.

records.context: **Assumption tests have their own power.** With n = 3, Levene's test has almost no power, so "p = 0.7" means the variances could not be compared, not that they are equal. records.context: 1. **A guessed mapping applied without review.** Their ``Area`` in µm² written into spaCR's ``cell_area`` in px² is a number that is wrong by a factor of a few hundred and looks completely plausible. So :func:`infer_column_map` only ever *proposes*; the proposal is a file the user edits (:func:`save_column_map` / :func:`load_column_map`); and :func:`run_import` applies what was agreed, nothing else. 2. **Units.** spaCR's intensities are raw uncalibrated counts, and its geometry is px²/px for a 2-D run — but a 3-D run measures volumes, in µm³ when it was given voxel_size_z_um/voxel_size_xy_um, under the same column names; the row's ``measurement_units`` says which, and :mod:`spacr.feature_dict` resolves it per table. A foreign table in µm needs a scale factor unless the target rows are µm too, and every mapping therefore carries ``unit_in`` / ``unit_out``. When a conversion is declared but the pixel size is unknown, the value is **not** multiplied by 1.0 and pretended to be pixels: the column is redirected to the ``foreign_`` prefix, recorded with its own unit and ``calibrated = 0``, and named in the plan and the summary. 3. **Columns that could not be mapped.** They are listed by name in the plan, in :meth:`ImportResult.summary`, and in the ``foreign_columns`` table — and they are still *imported*, under the ``foreign_`` prefix. No column is dropped silently. 4. **Name collisions.** A foreign column called ``cell_area`` that means something else would corrupt every downstream analysis with no error at all. Targets are checked against :func:`spacr.feature_dict.parse_column` and against spaCR's reserved identifier columns; a collision is a :class:`Conflict` that either refuses the import (``on_conflict='refuse'``, the default) or renames the column (``on_conflict='rename'``) — never an overwrite. 5. **A destination that is already somebody's project.** The same argument one level up: a *table* collision. See below.
records.label: spacr.foreign#7

records.context: **1. The Spacing is built from the SPACE axes only.** A 5-d ngff image has axes ``(t, c, z, y, x)``: the time axis is in seconds, the image data channel axis has no unit at all, and z/y/x are in micrometers. A single ``Spacing`` over all five would have to answer "what unit is this?" with one string, and whatever it answered would be wrong for three of the axes — a stack whose spacing claims ``"um"`` while one of its axes steps in seconds passes the unit check in ``layers.py`` and is then drawn at the wrong scale. So :attr:`OmeZarrImage.spacing` covers z/y/x, and t and c are reported alongside as :class:`Axis` records through :attr:`OmeZarrImage.other_axes`, :attr:`OmeZarrImage.time_axis` and :attr:`OmeZarrImage.channel_axis`. Nothing is lost; the reader does not treat seconds and micrometers as the same kind of number.

records.context: The writer builds a pyramid by **2x block mean over the two fastest-varying space axes** (see :func:`write_ome_zarr`). It is a box filter and **not a Gaussian pyramid**: there is no pre-filter beyond the box, so it aliases where a properly filtered pyramid would not. It is chosen anyway because it is separable, exact, dependency-free, and the same ``local_mean`` the rest of the NGFF ecosystem writes — matching what other viewers produce matters more here than a marginally better kernel. Striding (``downsample="stride"``) is offered and is **mandatory for label/mask arrays**: the mean of labels 3 and 5 is 4, an object that does not exist.

records.context: Level *k*'s ``scale`` is level 0's ``scale`` multiplied by the cumulative factor 2^k on each downsampled axis. records.context: **Why there is a cap.** A spaCR object table has 300-600 columns. A MapAnnotation with 400 entries renders in OMERO.web as a 400-row scrolling table in a 300 px panel, which hides the annotations worth showing. So the annotation is a *summary*, capped at ``max_pairs`` (:data:`MAX_MAP_PAIRS` = 50 by default) and ordered so the useful structured-data names are the ones that survive: ``priority`` structured-data names first in the order given, then the row's own order. records.context: 1. **Intervals are too narrow.** Mean-field VI systematically *underestimates* posterior variance, because it cannot represent posterior correlations and pays no penalty for ignoring them.  Treat ``q5``/``q95`` from the torch backend as a spread indicator, not as a calibrated 90 % interval, and never quote them as one in a paper. 2. **Convergence diagnostics are limited.** There is no R-hat and no effective sample size.  The only criterion is whether the ELBO stopped changing, which is reported as :attr:`PowerFit.converged` and is a much weaker claim than NUTS convergence. 3. **It can land in a local optimum**, and the horseshoe's funnel geometry is exactly the sort of thing that causes it. 4. **The posterior mean of beta — the ranking statistic — is the part that survives.** AUROC and average precision depend only on the *order* of the ``beta`` estimates, and that ordering is what mean-field VI gets right even when it gets the spread wrong.  This is why ADVI is a defensible default *for statistical detection sensitivity analysis specifically*, and why it is not a defensible default for reporting a per-gene credible interval.
records.label: spacr.power_model#16

Eina viðmiðið er hvort ELBO hætti að breytast, sem er birt sem :attr:`PowerFit.converged` og er mun veikari fullyrðing en samleitni NUTS. 3. **Aðferðin getur lent í staðbundnu kjörgildi**, og trektarlögun horseshoe-dreifingarinnar er nákvæmlega sú gerð lögunar sem veldur því. 4. **Eftirá-meðaltal beta — stærðin sem er notuð til röðunar — er sá hluti sem heldur gildi sínu.** AUROC og meðaltalsnákvæmni ráðast aðeins af *röð* ``beta`` matanna, og mean-field VI nær þeirri röð rétt jafnvel þegar matið á dreifingunni er rangt. records.context: The consequence that is *not* obvious, and is much larger, is what it does to the genes that were never testable. A gene that landed in every microplate sample position, or in none, has a constant read-fraction column; its coefficient is confounded with the intercept and ``power_model.prepare_model_data`` reports it as unidentified rather than as a non-hit. That check is what keeps a thin design from reporting untestable genes as negative results, and mis-assignment defeats it, because phantom reads give every gene a covariate that *varies*. records.context: Some thresholds are not offered here. Local mean and local Gaussian thresholding are not offered again: they are the Adaptive threshold mode, which runs the organelle engine's ``adaptive`` branch with a block size and an offset. Local OTSU is not offered again either: it is the "Local threshold (uneven illumination)" switch in plain Otsu mode, used by whole-image detection. Other named thresholds ignore saved Local Otsu and class-count settings; Multi-Otsu alone uses the selected class count and band in both scopes. Plain Otsu retains its legacy magnifier preprocessing, while the other thresholds use the whole-image engine on the requested extracted image region. Niblack uses ``T = m - k*s``; Sauvola uses ``T = m*(1 + k*(s/R - 1))``, where ``m`` and ``s`` are the local mean and standard deviation. The engine supplies float32 values without rescaling their range, so scikit-image's default Sauvola ``R`` is 1. These formulas are different, and changing the intensity scale can change Sauvola's result.

records.context: The disclosure level is changed only when necessary, and the change is not remembered. Switching to All settings unconditionally would work, and it would also rewrite this module's remembered Essentials/All choice every time anybody arrived here -- a setting the user chose, changed as a side effect of looking something up. So the filter is cleared first and the level is raised only when the row is still not on the form afterwards, which is exactly the case where Essentials is what is hiding it; and the raise goes through :meth:`_show_all_without_remembering`, so the form shows the row while the store still holds the level the user picked. Most settings are not essentials, so a lookup that persisted the raise would move almost every module out of Essentials for good.

records.context: The two robust constants are *not* interchangeable, and the module keeps them separate. 1.4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) is ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)``, the factor that makes the MAD of a normal sample an unbiased estimate of its SD. A moving range is ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, the absolute value of a *difference* of two observations, so its scale is ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` and its median is ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplying a median moving range by 1.4826 overestimates sigma by exactly ``sqrt(2)``, which makes the limits 41% wider and can hide a drift. Both constants are computed from ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` here for the same reason c4 is computed from the gamma function.

records.context: The profile is the default for one reason that outweighs its cost: **the Wald interval is finite by construction.** It is ``L ± t·SE``, so it returns a finite, symmetric interval even for a curve whose midpoint the data does not locate at all. The profile interval can *fail to close*: the residual sum of squares stays under the threshold all the way out to a concentration ten thousand times the highest dose tested, and that failure is the diagnostic. It is reported as an open bound, not smoothed into a number.

records.context: So the microplate sample position pass is **not** "the microplate sample position contains many flagged objects". The microplate sample position-level robust score finds the uniform shift while being blind to the isolated catastrophe. Both are on the microplate sample position frame because neither subsumes the other.

records.source: So the well pass is **not** "the well contains many flagged objects". records.translation: Samanburður brunna merkir því **ekki** „brunnurinn inniheldur marga merkta hluti“. Sú mælistærð er til — hún er birt sem ``flagged_share`` — en svarar annarri spurningu: hún finnur brunn með fáeinum *stórfelldum* frávikum (hruni í myndskiptingu eða rykkorni sem mældist sem fruma) en sér ekki samræmda hliðrun. records.context: The alternative considered and not taken is the Rousseeuw–Croux ``Sn`` (``1.1926 * med_i med_j |x_i - x_j|``), which is the statistically better answer: it has a 50% breakdown point, needs no symmetry assumption, and does not collapse on tied data. It is not used because the naive form is O(n^2) — unusable on the 10^5–10^6 object rows spaCR routinely produces — and the O(n log n) algorithm is a page of intricate code to maintain for a path that is only ever reached when the MAD has *already* collapsed. The mean absolute deviation has a 0% breakdown point and that is stated plainly rather than glossed: it is a stopgap that keeps a degenerate column from flagging its whole tail, not a robust estimator. If the fallback fires, the column is probably not continuous enough for this test.

records.context: **A file that exists is not a file that finished.** Older versions of ``spacr.io._load_and_concatenate_arrays`` wrote ``merged/<field>.npy`` with a bare ``np.save`` straight onto the destination path, so a crash mid-write left a short, structurally valid-looking ``.npy`` on disk. Current versions write merged arrays atomically, but files left by earlier runs can still be truncated. A resume that skips on ``os.path.exists`` would accept such a field, measure whatever bytes happened to land, and put the result in the same table as the good fields. So :func:`completed_fields_in_merged` *validates*: it parses the ``.npy`` header and checks that the file is as long as its own shape claims. Current versions write merged arrays atomically, but files left by earlier runs can still be truncated. A resume that skips on ``os.path.exists`` would accept such a field, measure whatever bytes happened to land, and put the result in the same table as the good fields. So :func:`completed_fields_in_merged` *validates*: it parses the ``.npy`` header and checks that the file is as long as its own shape claims. Anything short is reported as rejected and re-queued, never skipped.

Hrun í miðri skrifun skildi því eftir of stutta ``.npy`` á diski sem virtist hafa gilt snið. Núverandi útgáfur skrifa sameinuð fylki í einni ódeilanlegri aðgerð, en skrár frá fyrri keyrslum geta enn verið styttar. Framhald sem sleppti skrám út frá ``os.path.exists`` myndi samþykkja slíkt myndsvið, mæla þau bæti sem náðu að vistast og setja niðurstöðuna í sömu töflu og réttu myndsviðin. Allt sem er of stutt er tilkynnt sem hafnað og sett aftur í biðröð, aldrei sleppt.

When spaCR then measures the same field, :func:`_merge_and_save_to_database` *appends*: the measured rows are added beside the imported ones, in different columns, with nothing in the row to distinguish them, and every downstream ``count_cell`` becomes the sum of two populations.
records.translation: ``foreign.run_import`` afritar innfluttu gagnatöfluna í stöðluðu töfluna ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` þegar áfangastaðurinn er tómur, svo verkefni sem er eingöngu byggt á innflutningi sé læsilegt fyrir öll spaCR-verkfæri. Þegar spaCR mælir síðan sama myndsvið *bætir* :func:`_merge_and_save_to_database` við: mældu raðirnar koma við hlið innfluttu raðanna, í öðrum dálkum, án nokkurs í röðinni sem aðgreinir þær, og hvert ``count_cell`` í síðari vinnslu verður summa tveggja þýða.

records.context: Parameters: df (pd.DataFrame): The input DataFrame. group_col (str): Column name to group by, or a list of column names. Grouping passes ``observed=False``, so unused categories of a Categorical are kept. Rows whose group structured-data name is missing get a ``NaN`` per-row bound, because pandas drops ``NaN`` group structured-data names; they are discarded under 'iqr' and kept under 'zscore'. value_col (str): Column containing values to check for outliers. A name that is not in the frame raises ``KeyError``. method (str): 'iqr' or 'zscore'. Anything else raises ``ValueError``. The two agree on tiny groups: a one-row group has an undefined standard deviation, and since one row cannot be an outlier within its own group it is KEPT under both. threshold (float): Multiplier on the IQR (default 1.5), or the z-score cutoff. Must be >= 0; a negative value inverts the keep-band and raises ``ValueError``, because under 'iqr' it would empty every group with a nonzero IQR. ``0`` under 'zscore' keeps only rows sitting exactly on the group mean. Under 'zscore' an outlier inflates its own group's standard deviation, so the usual cutoffs keep more rows than 'iqr' does on the same data.

Grouping passes ``observed=False``, so unused categories of a Categorical are kept. Rows whose group key is missing get a ``NaN`` per-row bound, because pandas drops ``NaN`` group keys; they are discarded under 'iqr' and kept under 'zscore'. value_col (str): Column containing values to check for outliers. A name that is not in the frame raises ``KeyError``. method (str): 'iqr' or 'zscore'. Anything else raises ``ValueError``. The two agree on tiny groups: a one-row group has an undefined standard deviation, and since one row cannot be an outlier within its own group it is KEPT under both. threshold (float): Multiplier on the IQR (default 1.5), or the z-score cutoff. Must be >= 0; a negative value inverts the keep-band and raises ``ValueError``, because under 'iqr' it would empty every group with a nonzero IQR. ``0`` under 'zscore' keeps only rows sitting exactly on the group mean. Under 'zscore' an outlier inflates its own group's standard deviation, so the usual cutoffs keep more rows than 'iqr' does on the same data.
records.translation: Viðföng: df (pd.DataFrame): Inntakstaflan (DataFrame). group_col (str): Heiti dálks sem hópa skal eftir eða listi dálkaheita. Hópunin sendir ``observed=False``, svo ónotaðir flokkar í Categorical haldist. Raðir sem vantar hóplykil fá ``NaN``-mörk fyrir hverja röð, því pandas sleppir ``NaN``-hóplyklum; þeim er sleppt með 'iqr' en þær haldast með 'zscore'. value_col (str): Dálkur með gildum sem leita skal að útlögum í. Heiti sem er ekki í töflunni veldur ``KeyError``. method (str): 'iqr' eða 'zscore'. Allt annað veldur ``ValueError``. Aðferðirnar eru sammála um örsmáa hópa: staðalfrávik hóps með einni röð er óskilgreint og þar sem ein röð getur ekki verið útlagi innan eigin hóps er henni HALDIÐ með báðum. threshold (float): Margfaldari á IQR (sjálfgefið 1.5) eða þröskuldur fyrir z-gildi. Verður að vera >= 0; neikvætt gildi snýr við varðveislubilinu og veldur ``ValueError``, því með 'iqr' myndi það tæma alla hópa þar sem IQR er ekki núll. ``0`` með 'zscore' heldur aðeins röðum sem eru nákvæmlega við meðaltal hópsins. Með 'zscore' hækkar útlagi staðalfrávik eigin hóps, svo venjulegir þröskuldar halda fleiri röðum en 'iqr' gerir fyrir sömu gögn.

records.context: **All or nothing.** SQLite's DDL *is* transactional, but Python's sqlite3 driver only opens an implicit transaction for DML (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/ REPLACE) — an ``ALTER TABLE`` runs in autocommit and lands immediately. The transaction is therefore opened explicitly and rolled back on any error, so a call that raises applies no rename, and the connection is closed in a ``finally``.
records.label: spacr.utils.rename_columns_in_db#4

The transaction is therefore opened explicitly and rolled back on any error, so a call that raises applies no rename, and the connection is closed in a ``finally``.
records.translation: **Allt eða ekkert.** DDL í SQLite *er* færslutengt, en sqlite3-rekill Python opnar aðeins sjálfvirka færslu fyrir DML (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/ REPLACE) — ``ALTER TABLE`` keyrir með autocommit og tekur gildi strax. Færslan er því opnuð sérstaklega og afturkölluð við hverja villu. Kall sem kastar villu framkvæmir því enga endurnefningu og tengingunni er lokað í ``finally``.
